content.body:
The Stuart M3 series of light tanks was fast and carried the best 37mm AT gun of the war, which while small in caliber against those it faced, did reasonably well early in its career due to an extremely high muzzle velocity. The M3A3 and M5A1 (functionally similar) Stuarts were lend-leased to the Free French, and were found to perform very satisfactorily. By later war years, there were outclassed as the turret ring prevented bigger gun upgrades.
Control Variations: Driver has no viewslit, periscope only (numpad . or Del key). Driver can unbutton with O key. Driver has gauge showing turret direction relative to hull. Crew 4 is radioman, has hull mg with no crosshair at all. Can unbutton with the O key and still fire hull mg.
Fast. This thing is fast, with good turret rotation and a nicely powerful gun (with good optics) its a tank which acts like an armored car. Engage and move, engage and move. When you move, move in cover and behind crest-lines to deny the enemy the long shots (which have a good chance of killing you if they hit, almost regardless of caliber) as your armour is thin. Dont be mistaken that this is a main battle tank; its an excellent tank for sweeping around the edges of the enemy, picking off targets of opportunity.
Once in a while you can even get away with a dash up close but never stop moving and firing or you will get caught and killed quickly.
content.brief: TYPE: Light/Medium AFV ARMAMENT: 37mm HV Main gun 2 x .30 caliber LMG WEIGHT: 14415 kg SPEED (road): 58 km/h
content.title: Stuart M3A3
